## Binding Plan addendum — capability schema and target chronology

This addendum replaces only the two unresolved parts of the replacement Plan. All other sections remain settled.

### Blocker 1 — freeze the capability contract

#### Behavior

Reviewer activation has one mandatory authorization transport:

```text
--ak-review-capabilities <json-path>
```

The referenced file is UTF-8 JSON with exactly this version-1 schema (`additionalProperties: false` at every object level):

```ts
type ReviewerCapabilitiesV1 = Readonly<{
  version: 1;
  taskSha256: string; // exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters
  tools: readonly ReviewerChildToolName[];
  bashCommands: readonly string[];
  prerequisiteOperations: readonly ReviewerPrerequisiteOperation[];
}>;

type ReviewerChildToolName =
  | "read" | "grep" | "find" | "ls" | "bash" | "write" | "edit";

type ReviewerPrerequisiteOperation =
  // dispatch-owned, pre-acceptance Git identity/read operations
  | "preflight.git.pin-target"
  | "preflight.git.resolve-base"
  | "preflight.git.derive-range"
  | "preflight.git.list-ordered-commits"
  | "preflight.git.read-material"
  // runner-owned, post-acceptance Git setup/verification operations
  | "runner.git.materialize-mirror"
  | "runner.git.materialize-workspace"
  | "runner.git.verify-snapshot";
```

All three arrays are required, may be empty, contain no duplicates, and admit only the closed values above. `taskSha256` is SHA-256 over the exact existing `--ak-review-task` file bytes—not trimmed text, decoded/re-encoded text, a path, or proposal prose. Activation reads those bytes once, verifies the digest before exposing Reviewer tools, and thereafter uses the same bytes as the opaque task input. Missing flags/files, unreadable files, malformed JSON/UTF-8, wrong version/keys/types/digest casing, duplicate entries, unknown entries, or digest mismatch fail Reviewer activation/preflight. There is no implicit/default capability document, legacy fallback, empty-file interpretation, task-prose authority, or widening to host availability.

Each `bashCommands` member is the exact complete `command` string accepted by the child `bash` tool. Authorization is byte-for-byte JavaScript string equality against an accepted member. No trim, normalization, glob, prefix, regex, tokenization, argv parsing, quoting interpretation, shell inference, or task-text interpretation occurs. `bashCommands` must be empty unless `tools` contains `bash`; granting `bash` with an empty command array exposes the tool but permits no command. A command entry does not itself grant `bash`.

Proposal requirements retain the settled per-axis shape. For each accepted leg, effective child tools, exact bash strings, and package prerequisite operations equal that leg’s declared requirement after proving it is a subset of this task-bound ceiling and current host availability; they are never the entire ceiling by default. Common preflight requirements are checked against the ceiling before performing them; accepted runner setup requirements are the union required by the recipe and accepted legs. The closed prerequisite enum authorizes only package implementation operations at those named seams. It does not create child-visible commands or a generic filesystem, network, process, path, or sandbox policy.

The operation meanings are frozen as follows:

- `preflight.git.pin-target`: identify repository root and pin HEAD commit plus the review ref map/object identities before proposals are handled.
- `preflight.git.resolve-base`: resolve the declared base commit only within the immutable pin.
- `preflight.git.derive-range`: verify base ancestry/reachability and derive the canonical base-to-target range/diff identity.
- `preflight.git.list-ordered-commits`: obtain the deterministic ordered commits for that range.
- `preflight.git.read-material`: read proposal-selected repository material bytes from the pinned target/base identity; it grants no arbitrary working-tree read.
- `runner.git.materialize-mirror`: after acceptance, create/populate the accepted immutable mirror from the pin.
- `runner.git.materialize-workspace`: after acceptance, create each isolated writable leg workspace at the accepted target.
- `runner.git.verify-snapshot`: verify materialized HEAD, refs, and required objects against accepted pinned evidence.

#### Owner

`extensions/role-runtime.ts`/`src/reviewer-role.ts` register and load the mandatory flag through a narrow raw-byte loader. `src/reviewer-dispatch.ts` validates schema/digest, checks proposal subsets and host availability, and compiles immutable effective grants. `src/reviewer-agent.ts` enforces accepted child-tool visibility and exact bash-string equality and performs only accepted runner-prefixed operations. Task prose, the role adapter, and the runner never calculate or widen authority.

#### Red

Owning tests first reject: absent capability flag; missing/unreadable file; invalid UTF-8/JSON; extra keys; version other than `1`; uppercase/non-64-byte digest; a digest of trimmed task text; task mutation after digest/load; unknown/duplicate tools or operations; duplicate bash strings; command without `bash`; proposal requirement outside ceiling/host availability; and task prose claiming a wider grant. Bash tests prove `"git status"` does not authorize leading/trailing whitespace, extra flags, prefixes/suffixes, alternate quoting, shell composition, or any other string. Operation tests prove preflight names cannot authorize mirror/workspace setup and runner names cannot authorize target resolution/material reads.

#### Green

A valid task-digest-bound V1 document yields only exact proposal-subset grants. Children see only the accepted names from the seven-name vocabulary, and `bash` executes only exact accepted complete strings. Dispatch and runner can invoke only their respective closed prerequisite operations.

#### Scope and test ownership

Schema/digest/subset/enum tests belong to new `test/reviewer-dispatch.test.ts`; CLI loading/default failure belongs to `test/reviewer-role.test.ts` and `test/package-entrypoint.integration.test.ts`; visible-tool and exact-command enforcement belongs to `test/reviewer-agent.test.ts`; package lifecycle has one end-to-end valid file plus missing/mismatch refusal cases. Do not add aliases, `--ak-review-input`, generic policy vocabulary, task-prose parsing, or Soul text.

### Blocker 2 — freeze target chronology and ownership

#### Behavior

The irreversible sequence is:

1. **Activation pin:** before proposal handling is enabled, Reviewer runtime pins repository root, target HEAD, ref map, and required object identities. This immutable `RuntimePinnedTarget` is the only target authority for the invocation. No mirror or leg workspace is created.
2. **Proposal preflight reads:** while lifecycle remains `open`, `reviewer-dispatch` uses a narrow `ReviewerPinnedGitReader` against that pin to resolve the proposal’s declared base, prove reachability, derive canonical range/diff identity and ordered commits, and read exact selected material bytes. The adapter exposes only the five `preflight.git.*` operations above and rejects data not reachable in the pin; it cannot clone, create a workspace, invoke a provider, or start a child.
3. **Compile and validate:** dispatch compiles both required legs—or the one complete Standards leg for established no-spec—from the exact pinned evidence/task/Skill/material bytes, computes prompt identities and effective grants, reproduces them, and validates the entire candidate atomically.
4. **Reject or accept:** rejection records typed proposal identity/violations and no-start facts, leaves lifecycle `open`, and permits correction. These bounded Git identity/read operations are allowed on rejected attempts, but rejection creates no mirror/workspace, invokes no provider, starts no child, and consumes no batch. Acceptance deep-freezes target/base/range/ordered-commit/material evidence, exact compiled prompt bytes/hashes/lengths, grants, recipe identity, and cardinality, then records the sole irreversible `open → accepted-and-started` transition.
5. **Post-acceptance materialization/execution:** only after that transition does `reviewer-agent` receive the opaque `AcceptedReviewerDispatch`. It materializes/verifies the mirror and one or two workspaces from accepted pinned evidence, exposes accepted child grants, and sends accepted prompt bytes unchanged. It never resolves a base/target/material, derives a range, reads proposal materials, compiles/recompiles prompts, intersects grants, accepts/rejects proposals, or decides/reopens lifecycle.

The activation pin is identity capture/read-only Git work, not runner snapshot preparation. “Snapshot preparation” in the prior Plan is therefore split and renamed: dispatch-side immutable pin/read preflight occurs before acceptance; runner-side mirror/workspace materialization occurs only after acceptance. Accepted-and-started records the irreversible dispatch commitment before setup begins; setup/provider failure is post-acceptance infrastructure evidence and cannot reopen correction or permit another batch.

#### Owner

`reviewer-dispatch` owns the pin-reader interface, base/range/commit/material resolution, compilation, grant validation, rejection/acceptance, and sole transition. A package Git adapter implements only pin-bound reads. `reviewer-agent` owns mirror/workspace materialization, snapshot verification, provider/session mechanics, and opaque execution after transition. The ledger remains an append-only projection and owns neither sequence nor decisions; role/runtime wiring only constructs these dependencies.

#### Red

A fake chronology test proves activation pin precedes tool availability. Rejected proposals may increment only pin-reader calls and ledger rejection events; assertions require zero `mkdtemp`, clone/fetch/workspace, provider, session, child-start, and batch-consumption calls. Counterexamples reject a base/material outside the pin, ref/HEAD drift, inconsistent range, changed material bytes, or a missing preflight operation. Tests make runner methods fail if called before acceptance and make accepted opaque inputs impossible to reinterpret. They also prove runner setup failure occurs after the irreversible transition and does not allow correction, and prove the runner has no target resolver/compiler/grant/lifecycle dependency.

#### Green

A corrected proposal can follow any number of bounded read-only rejections, accept exactly once with frozen evidence, and only then cause one accepted Standards workspace/child or two isolated overlapping Standards/Spec workspaces/children. Materialized HEAD/refs/objects and provider-facing prompt bytes exactly match accepted evidence.

#### Scope and test ownership

Pin-reader and state-order tests belong to `test/reviewer-dispatch.test.ts`; mirror/workspace post-acceptance and opaque-runner tests belong to `test/reviewer-agent.test.ts`; append-only ordering/no-start evidence belongs to `test/reviewer-execution-ledger.test.ts`; one rejection-then-correction and both accepted cardinalities belong to `test/reviewer-package-lifecycle.test.ts`. Replace contradictory old assertions that every rejection performs zero snapshot reads with the precise rule: bounded immutable pin reads are permitted, while materialization/provider/child/batch effects remain zero. No second snapshot authority, pre-acceptance mirror, caller-supplied bytes, runner-side resolution, or parallel lifecycle seam is introduced.
